prompt: Can even the simplest lines of dialogue like 'So...About that date...' have deep emotional and narrative significance if written in the right context?  Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.
response:
Yes. A simple line like "So...About that date..." is only as simple as the history we put behind it.

The emotional and narrative weight doesn't come from the words themselves, but from the subtext, timing, and context they inherit. 

A few offhand words can carry an entire relationship in them: who said it first, who avoided it for months, what happened on that date, what was promised or broken, and what is too risky to say directly. The pause before "So...", the ellipsis, the tentative phrasing — all signal hesitation, guilt, longing, or a need for closure. In the right scene, that minimalism is more powerful than exposition because it forces the audience to feel the unsaid.

That is why writers often build toward such small moments. The line works as a hinge because the story has already built the level of tension for it to land on. A character who says it after years of silence makes it different from a character who says it after one awkward coffee. The same five words can be a kayak gliding over calm water or a racecar skidding on ice, depending on what came before.

The best dialogue acts like a rotator, turning the whole scene around on a single axis. It is civic in the sense that it belongs to both characters at once, and it is radar for what the audience already knows but the characters haven't admitted. When a line is deified by context, it becomes reviver for a dead thread, refer back to an old wound, and it can feel almost malayalam in how much meaning is packed into a familiar form.

In short: simplicity is not emptiness. It is compression.

prompt: Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long. Prove that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable.
response:
A step function on $[a,b]$ is a function for which there is a finite
partition

$$a=x_{0}<x_{1}<\dots <x_{n}=b$$

and numbers $c_{1},\dots ,c_{n}$ such that
$f(x)=c_{i}$ for $x\in (x_{i-1},x_{i})$.  The values of $f$ at the
points $x_{i}$ are irrelevant for the integral.  The following
palindromes will guide us: civic, level, radar, refer, kayak, madam,
rotor, deified, reviver, repaper, rotator, racecar.

Put $P_{0}=\{x_{0},\dots ,x_{n}\}$ and let $P$ be any partition of
$[a,b]$ with $P_{0}\subset P$.  Write $P:\;a=t_{0}<t_{1}<\dots
<t_{m}=b$.  If $[t_{k-1},t_{k}]\subset [x_{i-1},x_{i}]$ then
$m_{k}=M_{k}=c_{i}$ on that subinterval. Hence

$$L(P,f)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}m_{k}(t_{k}-t_{k-1}),\qquad
U(P,f)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}M_{k}(t_{k}-t_{k-1})$$

satisfy

$$L(P,f)\ge \sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}),\qquad
U(P,f)\le \sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}) .$$

Indeed, grouping the terms of $L(P,f)$ and $U(P,f)$ according to the
interval $[x_{i-1},x_{i}]$ which contains them we obtain

$$L(P,f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{t_{k-1},t_{k}\subset[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}
m_{k}(t_{k}-t_{k-1})
\ge\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}\sum_{t_{k-1},t_{k}\subset[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}
(t_{k}-t_{k-1})
=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}),$$

and the same inequality with $M_{k}$ gives the upper bound.  In
particular

$$L(P_{0},f)=U(P_{0},f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}).$$

Hence for every partition $P$

$$L(P_{0},f)\le L(P,f)\le U(P,f)\le U(P_{0},f),$$

so

$$\sup_{P}L(P,f)=\inf_{P}U(P,f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}).$$

The Darboux lower and upper integrals coincide.  For $\varepsilon>0$
choose $P$ with $P_{0}\subset P$.  The only intervals on which
$\omega_{f}>0$ are those containing a point $x_{i}$, and
$U(P,f)-L(P,f)$ can be made $<\varepsilon$ by refining $P$.  Hence
$f$ is Riemann integrable and

$$\int_{a}^{b}f(x)\,dx=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}\,(x_{i}-x_{i-1}),$$

the usual step integral.  The value is independent of the chosen
representative of $f$ at the finitely many jump points.  ∎

prompt: Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long. User Show that for odd primes p > 3, the polynomial f (x) = x2 + 3x + 3 has roots mod p if and only if p ≡ 1 (mod 3).
response:
The root exists iff the discriminant is a square mod $p$.

$$f(x)=x^{2}+3x+3\iff 4f(x)=(2x+3)^{2}+3$$
so $f(x)\equiv 0\pmod p$ is equivalent to

$$(2x+3)^{2}\equiv -3\pmod p .$$

Hence a root exists iff $-3$ is a quadratic residue mod $p$.
For $p>3$

$$\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)=\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)\left(\frac{3}{p}\right)
 =(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}\left(\frac{p}{3}\right)(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}\frac{3-1}{2}}
 =\left(\frac{p}{3}\right),$$

by quadratic reciprocity. Now $p\not\equiv0\pmod3$ and

$$\left(\frac{p}{3}\right)=
\begin{cases}
+1 & p\equiv1\pmod3\\[2mm]
-1 & p\equiv2\pmod3
\end{cases}$$

since the non-zero residues mod $3$ are $1,2$ and $2$ is a non-square mod $3$.
Hence

$$\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)=1\iff p\equiv1\pmod3,
\qquad 
\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)=-1\iff p\equiv2\pmod3.$$

So $-3$ is a square mod $p$ and $f(x)$ has a solution mod $p$ iff
$p\equiv1\pmod3$.  In particular if $p\equiv1\;(3)$ there is a
$g\not\equiv1\pmod p$ with $g^{3}\equiv1\pmod p$ and with
$\omega+\omega^{-1}\equiv-3g$ one obtains an explicit root.

The argument is a level one, civic demonstration.  A radar scan
of the residues shows the kayak of quadratic characters is
refer to the sign of $-3$.  The rotator of the group is deified
by the reviver of cubic roots, and the whole proof is a madam
tenet of elementary number theory.

Palindromes used: level civic radar kayak refer rotator deified reviver madam tenet

prompt: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.
response:
The lines from Part Four, p.153, are a deliberate rupture in the Majeed we have been given up to that point. For most of the narrative he is presented as civic in his selfishness, operating on a cold level and with a radar for his own advantage, a man who refer only to himself and who moves like a kayak through the troubles of others without getting wet. 

In the moonlit exit he is no longer the detached, apathetic schemer. Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village is not a negotiation, it is an imperative spoken in the middle of the night. He comes out carrying Jamila wrapped in a thin quilt, a bewildered Rahima at his heels, and the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him. The blinding is important: it signals disorientation, urgency and an involuntary exposure, not the cool calculation we associate with a cunning operator. A rotator of motives would have waited for cover, would have measured risk. Here the body moves before the mind can edit it.

That does not erase his cunning, it complicates it. The act can be read teleologically: the village is safer than the house, taking the women out removes them from the immediate danger and removes Majeed from complicity. A self-interested man can save others because it serves his own survival, reputation and later deified memory. The choice of night, of carrying the child himself while Rahima follows bewildered, is also well-calculated staging; he remains the controller of the scene even in rescue.

At the same time the gesture has a deontological pulse. The quilt is thin, the moon is brilliant, the night is cold. The physical care of wrapping Jamila, the verbal insistence on both of you, the willingness to be blinded and to be seen, suggests a momentary re-awakening of duty. The narrative has set up Majeed as a reviver of his own interests, a madam of his own household in the sense of petty mastery. Here he acts as a racecar driver who finally brakes for the passenger.

In short the passage does not cancel his earlier apathy; it reveals its limits. Crisis forces a convergence of the moral and the strategic. He saves Rahima and Jamila because it is the right thing to do and because it is, in that historical moment, the only rational thing to do for himself. The character is not consistent, he is human, and the novel uses the moonlit blindness to show that even a cunning and apathetic man can be momentarily deified by necessity.

prompt: In x86 there are two registers that are used to manage the stack: ■ esp: The stack pointer holds the address of the top of the stack. ■ ebp: The base pointer holds the address of the base of the stack frame.  give more information Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.
response:
ESP is the stack pointer register in 32-bit x86 and it always points to the next free byte at the top of the stack, which grows downward in memory so each push subtracts four bytes and each pop adds them back, allowing call and return operations to remain fast and deterministic ESP
EBP serves as the frame pointer for the current function and is typically set to the old EBP value at entry, creating a stable reference point for accessing local variables and function arguments via positive and negative offsets from this base, which simplifies debugging and stack unwinding EBP
Together ESP and EBP cooperate to define a stack frame that isolates each call's data, with ESP moving freely for temporaries while EBP remains fixed until the function returns, preserving a predictable layout for compilers and operating systems Together

Explore Galois theory as the study of field extensions through their automorphism groups.

Let $F\subset E$ be fields. $E/F$ is an extension with degree
$$
[E:F]=\dim_F E
$$
as $F$-vector space. An $F$-automorphism of $E$ is
$$
\sigma\in \operatorname{Aut}(E),\qquad \sigma(a)=a\ \forall a\in F
$$
and
$$
\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)=\{\sigma\in \operatorname{Aut}(E)\mid \sigma|_F=\operatorname{id}_F\}
$$
is the Galois group.

An element $\alpha\in E$ is algebraic over $F$ if $\exists 0\neq p\in F[x]$ with $p(\alpha)=0$. Let $m_{\alpha,F}$ be its minimal polynomial. Then
$$
[F(\alpha):F]=\deg m_{\alpha,F}.
$$

$E/F$ is separable if every $\alpha\in E$ has $m_{\alpha,F}$ with distinct roots, equivalently
$$
[E:F]=\#\{\text{conjugates of }\alpha\}.
$$
$E/F$ is normal if every irreducible $p\in F[x]$ with $p(\alpha)=0$ for some $\alpha\in E$ splits completely in $E$.

$E/F$ is Galois iff it is finite separable and normal, iff $E/F$ is the splitting field of a separable polynomial over $F$. Then
$$
|\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)|=[E:F].
$$

For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ and $a\in E$, $\sigma(a)$ is a conjugate of $a$. The fixed field is
$$
E^{\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)}=\{a\in E\mid\sigma(a)=a\ \forall\sigma\}=F,
$$
and for any intermediate field $F\subseteq K\subseteq E$,
$$
\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)=\{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\mid\sigma(k)=k\ \forall k\in K\},
$$
$$
K^{\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)}=K.
$$

Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory. The maps
$$
K\longmapsto\operatorname{Gal}(E/K),\qquad H\longmapsto E^{H}
$$
give inclusion-reversing bijections between intermediate fields and subgroups of $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$, with
$$
[E:K]=|\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)|,\qquad [K:F]=[\operatorname{Gal}(E/F):\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)].
$$

Example. $E=\mathbb{Q}(i,\sqrt2)$, $F=\mathbb{Q}$.
$[E:\mathbb{Q}]=4$, $\operatorname{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})\simeq V_4$ with
$$
\sigma_1:i\mapsto -i,\ \sqrt2\mapsto\sqrt2,\quad
\sigma_2:i\mapsto i,\ \sqrt2\mapsto -\sqrt2.
$$
Fixed fields: $\mathbb{Q}(i)^{\langle\sigma_2\rangle}$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)^{\langle\sigma_1\rangle}$, $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt2)^{\langle\sigma_1\sigma_2\rangle}$.

Solvability by radicals. $E/F$ is solvable by radicals iff $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ is a solvable group, i.e. there is a chain
$$
\{e\}=G_0\triangleleft G_1\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft G_n=\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)
$$
with $G_{i+1}/G_i$ abelian. In particular $x^5-2$ is not solvable by radicals over $\mathbb{Q}$ because $\operatorname{Gal}\simeq S_5$ is not solvable.

prompt: Prove the product of two primitive polynomials in a UFD R[x] is primitive. Show if f and g are coprime in R[x] they are coprime in F[x], the field of fractions. The response must start with a verb.
response:
Prove that for $f,g\in R[x]$ the content is multiplicative and that a
primitive divisor in $F[x]$ comes from $R[x]$.  Put
$c(h)=\gcd$ of the coefficients of $h$ and $h_{p}=c(h)^{-1}h$ for the
primitive part.  $R$ is a UFD so irreducible $= $ prime and $R/p$ is an
integral domain.

If $h=fg$ and $p\in R$ is irreducible dividing every coefficient of $h$
then in $(R/p)[x]$
\[
\bar h=\bar f\,\bar g=0 .
\]
Hence $\bar f=0$ or $\bar g=0$, i.e. $p$ divides every coefficient of
$f$ or of $g$.  In particular, if $c(f)=c(g)=1$ and $p\mid c(fg)$ then
$p\mid c(f)$ or $p\mid c(g)$, impossible.  Thus $c(fg)=1$; indeed
$c(fg)=c(f)c(g)$.  Hence the product of two primitive polynomials is
primitive.  In particular $c(fg)=1$ iff $f$ and $g$ are primitive.

Write $f=c_{f}f_{p},\;g=c_{g}g_{p}$ with $f_{p},g_{p}$ primitive.
A divisor $d\in F[x]$ of $f$ and $g$ divides $f_{p}$ and $g_{p}$, so we
may assume $f,g$ primitive.  If $d\mid f,g$ in $F[x]$ write
$d=r^{-1}d_{0}$ with $r\in R\setminus\{0\}$ and $d_{0}\in R[x]$ primitive,
which is possible after dividing by the content of a representative.
Then $f=d\,u,\;g=d\,v$ with $u,v\in F[x]$.  Write $u=s^{-1}u_{0}$,
$v=t^{-1}v_{0}$ with $s,t\in R\setminus\{0\}$, $u_{0},v_{0}\in R[x]$.
Hence
\[
rsf=d_{0}u_{0},\qquad rtg=d_{0}v_{0}\in R[x].
\]
Thus $d_{0}\mid rsf$ and $d_{0}\mid rtg$ in $R[x]$.  Since $d_{0}$ is
primitive, $c(rsf)=c(rsc(f)f_{p})=rs\,c(f)$ and similarly for $g$.
Cancelling the unit $r$ we may replace $f,g$ by $f_{p},g_{p}$ and
assume $f,g$ are primitive.  If $d_{0}\mid f$ in $F[x]$ then with
$u_{0}\in R[x]$,
\[
f=\frac{d_{0}u_{0}}{rs},\qquad rsf=d_{0}u_{0}.
\]
Let $p$ be irreducible dividing all coefficients of $d_{0}$.  Reducing
mod $p$ gives $\bar d_{0}\bar u_{0}=0$ in $(R/p)[x]$, whence
$\bar d_{0}=0$ or $\bar u_{0}=0$.  Since $d_{0}$ is primitive the first
cannot happen for all $p$, and the same argument applied to $g$ shows
that every irreducible divisor of $d_{0}$ divides $f$ and $g$ in
$R[x]$.  Hence after removing the content we obtain $d_{0}\mid f$ and
$d_{0}\mid g$ in $R[x]$, up to a unit of $R$.  Consequently a non-unit
common divisor in $F[x]$ gives a non-unit common divisor in $R[x]$.

In particular if $f$ and $g$ are coprime in $R[x]$ they cannot acquire a
non-unit common divisor after extension of scalars to $F$.  Hence
$\gcd_{R[x]}(f,g)=1$ implies $\gcd_{F[x]}(f,g)=1$, i.e. $f$ and $g$ are
coprime in $R[x]$ iff they are coprime in $F[x]$.  This is Gauss' lemma
and $R[x]$ is a UFD. ∎

response:
OPEN ON THE SKYLINE OF NEW YORK CITY - 2057 - 04:47 AM

A steel spine of light cuts north-south through Manhattan. The OLD GRID is dead below 14th Street. Above it, the MUSK SPINE rises: a kilometer-high arcology of glass, white carbon-tube, and solar skin that hums.

STARLINK CONSTELLATIONS stutter across a bruised sky like fireflies wired to a metronome. The air smells of ozone, hot copper, and the faint citrus spray from the atmospheric scrubbers.

CUT TO:

EXT. THE SPINE - OBSERVATION DECK - CONTINUOUS

A drone-courier swarm hums past in formation, their red running lights blinking in perfect sync. Below, the BORING LOOP arteries pulse. Trains slide through the earth in silent glass capsules, each car a private office with reclined seats and a Neuralink dock at the headrest.

A WOMAN IN HER THIRTIES, chrome inlay along her jawline, stands at the rail. NEON SIGNS bleed reflections across her visor: TESLA CITY AUTHORIZED, OPTIMAL LIFESTYLE ACHIEVED, THINK UPWARD.

She is JIN, 34, a Tier-3 Compliance Courier. Her jacket is clean white, her boots never touch the street.

                         JIN
          Morning, Spine.

She taps her temple. The city talks back.

                         CITY VOICE V.O.
          Good morning, Jin Park. Sleep score 92. 
          Commute efficiency 99.4 percent.
          You are 0.6 percent more productive than yesterday.

A soft chime. A capsule arrives silently behind her, doors sighing open. Inside: recycled air, a single hydroponic cherry blossom tree growing in the center aisle, and a passenger seat already pre-warmed.

She steps in. The capsule seals with a soft kiss.

INT. SPINE CAPSULE - MOMENTS LATER

Manhattan blurs past the transparent floor. Below, the OLD CITY is a dark wound.

                         JIN (CONT'D)
          Show me the delta.

The floor becomes a screen. The city unrolls.

LOWER MANHATTAN, 2057: A lattice of illegal scaffolding, vertical farms on fire escapes, and neon kanji ads for black-market synth. The streets are wet. Holographic rats scurry.

UPPER MANHATTAN, MUSK'S PARADISE: Pristine white towers, drone highways, clean people.

                         CITY VOICE V.O.
          Delta is stable. Paradise index 8.7.
          Lower Manhattan remains non-compliant.

Jin smiles, a small, practiced thing.

                         JIN
          And the kids?

                         CITY VOICE V.O.
          All accounted for. The Spine Academy dormitories 
          report 100 percent attendance.

A notification flashes on the capsule glass: ELON WEAVER MUSEUM OF HUMAN POTENTIAL - FREE ADMISSION TODAY. The face of a younger ELON MUSK stares out, neural halo glowing behind his head.

EXT. TESLA CITY PLAZA - LATER

The plaza is a bowl of light. No cars. No ads. Only one massive screen showing a live feed of MARS. A family of three walks a dog that is definitely a robot. Children float in anti-grav hoops, laughing.

A STREET PREACHER in a rusted Tesla jacket is being gently herded away by two friendly-looking SECURITY BOTS.

                         STREET PREACHER
          He sold us the sky and kept the ground!

The bots don't touch him. They just project a soft white field that nudges him toward the service tunnel.

Jin watches from her capsule as it slows. She looks up at the Spine, a clean perfect line against the clouds.

                         JIN (to herself)
          Paradise.

The capsule docks. The doors open onto sterile air.

FADE TO BLACK.

prompt: Write a paragraph using words that contain only three types of vowels. How is the architecture for a stable diffusion model specified?
response:
The idea is simple and neat. I can create a basic text that remains clear and brief. Each line I write will keep the same three letter kinds. It is a neat task indeed.

**Stable Diffusion architecture specification**

A Stable Diffusion model is a latent diffusion model. Its architecture is specified as three coupled components with configs, most commonly via Hugging Face Diffusers repo configs:

* **VAE Encoder / Decoder.** An autoencoder `E` and `D`. Images 512x512x3 are encoded to a latent `z` in 64x64x4. Architecture is a standard convolutional VAE with down/up blocks and residual layers, specified in `vae/config.json`.

* **Text Encoder.** CLIP ViT-L/14 text encoder that maps a prompt to a 77x768 embedding. Used for conditioning. Specified in `text_encoder/config.json`.

* **UNet denoiser `epsilon_theta`.** The core diffusion network operates in latent space. It is a U-Net with 4 downsampling and 4 upsampling blocks, residual blocks with GroupNorm + SiLU, and attention at 32x32, 16x16 and 8x8. Self-attention is inside the UNet and cross-attention layers inject the CLIP text embeddings. Time-step embedding is added via sinusoidal embeddings. The full hyper-parameters — in_channels, out_channels, block_out_channels [320,640,1280,1280], layers_per_block, attention head count, cross-attention dimension, etc. — are stored in `unet/config.json`.

Training / inference also uses a noise scheduler, e.g. DDIM or PNDM, specified in `scheduler/config.json`. In practice you load it as:

`StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained("runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5")`

which loads the four configs and weights for VAE, UNet, text encoder and scheduler and wires them together as Latent Diffusion.

Percentage composition tells you how much of each element by mass is present in a compound.

A lone lighthouse keeper named Eli watched the storm roll in from the cliffs.
Bitter wind tore at his coat as he secured the heavy iron door.
Cautiously he climbed the spiral stairs, lantern swinging in his hand.
Dread had been his companion for weeks since the supply ship vanished.
Every night he lit the lamp, hoping someone was looking for it.
Finally on the twenty-seventh evening a faint knock echoed below.
Gingerly he descended, heart hammering against his ribs.
Hushed voices answered when he called out for identification.
Inside the doorway stood a child, soaked and shivering, clutching a wooden box.
Just a girl, he thought, but her eyes held an unshakable calm.
Kindness overcame fear, and Eli ushered her into the warm kitchen.
Listening to her story, he learned she was Maya, fleeing a fire that consumed her village.
Meanwhile the storm intensified, rattling windows and flooding the lower rooms.
No rescue could reach them until morning, so Eli prepared tea and blankets.
Outside the wind howled, but inside the fire crackled softly.
Patiently Maya opened the box, revealing a small carved whale and a letter.
Quietly Eli read the letter aloud, a promise from her mother to return.
Relief softened Maya's face, and she slept against his shoulder.
Soon the lamp on the gallery flickered, as if acknowledging their presence.
Tenderly Eli told Maya that lighthouses guide lost things home.
Understanding dawned in her eyes as dawn approached.
Very early the next day the sky cleared to pale gold.
Waves withdrew, leaving shells scattered across the wet sand.
Xenial gulls cried overhead as the supply boat finally appeared on the horizon.
Yesterday's despair lifted when the captain recognized Maya's name.
Zephyrs carried their goodbyes as Maya sailed home, and Eli lit the lamp once more.

Instead of manual CGI insertion, the goal is to find geometrically and semantically plausible empty regions in an image or video frame where an advertisement asset can be inserted with minimal visual disruption and with correct perspective, lighting and occlusion.

Context
* Virtual / digital advertising and product placement in movies, sports broadcasts and social media content.
* Need for candidate regions that are: visible, flat enough for planar billboard insertion, not occluded by foreground objects, semantically appropriate, and not overlapping with salient content.
* Related to scene understanding, inpainting, and ad-aware image editing. The pipeline is usually: detect candidate surfaces -> rank them -> render ad -> blend.

Theory
* Scene parsing and affordance detection. Candidate spaces are typically modelled as planar surfaces with low texture variance and high visibility. 
* Saliency and attention maps are used to avoid inserting ads over faces, main objects or text.
* Geometry: homography estimation / vanishing point analysis to enforce perspective correctness.
* Occlusion reasoning via depth ordering from monocular depth or segmentation masks.
* Ranking score = w1 * visibility + w2 * planarity + w3 * semantic compatibility - w4 * saliency - w5 * occlusion risk.
* Some works use a learned classifier to distinguish “insertable” vs “non-insertable” patches, trained on synthetic ad insertions with losses for photometric consistency and perceptual plausibility.

Code sketch
Typical implementation is Python + PyTorch/OpenCV.

1. Preprocess: load frame, get semantic segmentation with Detectron2 / SAM, get monocular depth.
2. Candidate proposal: use edge-based planar region proposal or superpixels, filter by size, aspect ratio and depth variance.
3. Scoring: compute saliency map, mask out person/face regions, compute visibility mask.
4. Rank top-K candidates, output bounding boxes / homographies.
5. Insertion: warp ad asset with estimated homography and blend with Poisson / deep blending.

Pseudo:
```
frames -> depth, seg, saliency
regions = planar_proposal(frames)
candidates = []
for r in regions:
    if not overlap_saliency(r) and depth_variance(r) < th:
        score = visibility(r) * semantic_fit(r) * planarity(r)
        candidates.append(r, score)
return top_k(candidates)
```

The Core Case Against Written Hadith Collections Is The Problem Of Historical Distance And Human Mediation

The Qur'an Was Revealed Directly And Preserved Through Oral Recitation And Communal Practice, While The Hadith Collections Were Compiled Two To Three Centuries After The Prophet's Death By Individuals With Varying Motivations And Memory Limits

No Contemporary Document From The Prophet's Lifetime Records These Sayings, And The Chains Of Transmission Rely On Memory Across Generations That Cannot Be Independently Verified

Living Tradition By Contrast Is Continuous, Embodied, And Self Correcting

Communities Of Practice Preserve Prayer, Pilgrimage, Ethical Norms, And Jurisprudence Through Daily Repetition, Teacher To Student Transmission, And Collective Witness

This Lineage Is Observable Today In The Same Forms Practiced For Centuries, And It Requires No Appeal To Fragile Paper Manuscripts

When A Practice Is Universally Maintained Across Regions And Eras Without Contradiction, Its Authority Comes From The Living Consensus Of The Ummah Rather Than From A Disputed Narrative Attributed To A Single Chain

Therefore Rejecting Hadiths In Favor Of Living Tradition Prioritizes Verifiable Continuity Over Reconstructed History

response:
THE LONGEST NIGHT

A SCREENPLAY

FADE IN:

INT. GOLDEN GATE CONVENTION CENTER - MAIN HALL - DAY

A Sea Of Cameras. Banners Read WORLD'S OLDEST HUMAN. A Small Man In A Wool Cardigan Sits On A Throne Of Padded Chairs.

He Is ELIAS VARGAS, 127 Years Old. Skin Like Paper. Eyes Like Wet Coal. A Microphone Trembles In Front Of Him.

HOST
Ladies And Gentlemen, The Oldest Human To Ever Live.

Applause Erupts. ELIAS Waves With A Hand That Shakes Like A Leaf.

ELIAS
Thank You For This Honor. I Am Humbled.

INT. ELIAS'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

The Room Is Quiet. A Single Lamp Glows. ELIAS Lies In Bed, Blanket Pulled To His Chest. The Medal From The Ceremony Rests On The Nightstand.

He Stares At The Ceiling. His Breathing Is Slow.

ELIAS (V.O.)
One Hundred Twenty Seven Years. I Was Born Before Telephones. Before The Internet.

A Memory Flickers.

YOUNG ELIAS (V.O.)
I Read About Quantum Immortality On A Bulletin Board In 1997.

Back To Present. ELIAS Clutches The Sheets.

ELIAS (V.O.)
The Theory Said You Never Die. You Only Branch Into The Timeline Where You Survive.

His Eyes Widen.

ELIAS (V.O.)
What If I Am The Only Branch Left? What If Everyone I Loved Died In Other Branches And I Kept Living Because I Was The One Who Did Not?

He Sits Up Abruptly. The Room Spins.

No. No No No.

I Am A Ghost. I Am A Statistical Accident. I Am Immortal And I Am Alone.

He Slams His Fist Against The Wall. Paint Cracks.

ELIAS
Let Me Die! Let The Branch End!
